A page nobody looked at, and every check passed it

It builds, it deploys, it answers 200, and there is no nav on it, no footer, and no anchor anywhere that goes back to the root. A reader who lands here has nowhere to go.

Prose that stops at half the measure

The two decisions that produce this are each correct on their own. Cap the measure so a line of prose is readable, and keep the block's left edge on the column every other section shares. Put them together and the page uses half of the width it has already established, down several screens, with nothing painted beside it.

Nothing overflows. Nothing clips. No contrast fails on this block, no label wraps, and every other check in a normal pipeline passes it. The page simply reads as unbuilt, and the only way to know is to look at it.

The measurement is the page against itself. There is no width a block is supposed to be, so the reference is this document's own ninetieth-percentile content edge, and a run of rows is reported when it stops far short of that edge while still starting on the page's normal left margin. A block centred in the same frame is left alone, because the slack is split and the page reads as composed.

This block runs long enough to clear the run floor, which is two hundred and forty pixels of contiguous dead height. A short band under a heading is not this defect and is not reported as one, which is why the height counted is the dead rows themselves rather than the span from the first of them to the last.

Ink nobody can read

This paragraph is set in a grey that measures about two to one against the white behind it, which is under half of what WCAG 1.4.3 asks for at this size. It looks like a design decision in a screenshot and it is unreadable on a laptop in daylight.
